subtitle: The top 4 survived my fundamental + technical filter. I'm buying the #1
title: I ranked 37 stocks. Only ONE earned a Buy
description: The top 4 survived my fundamental + technical filter. I'm buying the #1
body_html:
Mid-week movers is where you give me stocks have that have peaked your interest…and then ranked from worst to first. You gave me 37 different tickers to sort through. The top 4 stocks all look outstanding!

No one wants to sit through 37 different stock reviews…sounds incredibly boring unless you are a true market masochist! We eliminated these stocks per fundamental rules first, and then eliminated through technical analysis. We need both fundamentals and technical aspects to align to achieve the highest probability of success, and returns.

Just because I rank a stock lower…DOES NOT MEAN THE STOCK CANNOT OR WILL NOT GO UP! I have to sort these, and choose the best with a rules based approach.

Rules

  1. Stock price must be above the 200 day moving average.

    1. You cannot achieve a 52-day high, a 52-week high…or even a local high if the stock price action is below the 200 day moving average. Period. Many think they are getting a discount…and maybe they are…but this is fighting trend and this is a bad long term habit. Because of this, these stocks were eliminated immediately:

      1. AFRM, MELI, NVO, PSTG, SOFI.

        1. Affirm hurts a little bit. This is one of my favorite companies from a fundamental standpoint. We made a small fortune from Affirm back in 2024 and a few times in 2025. But alas…price action does not want to cooperate. We can circle back another day.

  2. Annual Earnings Per Share (EPS) improving?

    1. It’s all about shareholder value. Period. Are shareholders making more money? Reliably? For these companies, the annual EPS had some form of decline:

      1. ALM, HII, NXT, POWL, USAR, VICR

        1. Huntington Ingalls, , was one of my favorite stocks just a few months ago, and I had an article featured on the Yahoo Finance Analysis page last September. The stock has ran more than +56% since that point. I think HII will continue to run…but because this is a rules based analysis, it must be placed lower on the list, regardless of my technical overview or emotional bias.

  3. The entire point of a business is to make money.

    1. If you start a company and start in debt…you need to make money. You hire employees…you need to make money. As a business, your entire purpose is to bring in money. And not just bring in money, bring in more and more year over year. Now to be clear, some of these companies are in fact bringing in money…but less than in prior years, which is a warning flag. Stick with me…this is rules based investing. The following companies either lost money, or made less money than prior years:

      1. ARWR, BAP, BE, COCO, COHR, ONDS, RY, TER, UPS, WWD

        1. Bloom Energy, , was a stock from the StockTok Screener and the number 1 stock from that screener, returning over +380%. We caught a portion of that. But certainly not all. That said, Energy is getting a lot of attention still and BE made a full recovery from the November to December Crash. This is still a company I would go long only right now…we are rules based investing though.

        2. Special shout out to the Vita Coco Company, that didn’t meet our fundamental rules, but had a really fantastic chart. The consistent lower highs, tight consolidation and recent breakout on 03 February…from a chart perspective, this ticker looks great.

  4. Are speculators speculating more and more?

    1. You can have a fantastic company. Great earnings. Great cash flow. But then sometimes… you look at the chart…and the price action is dying. All the fundamentals in the world matter not if the price action is down and there is no hope behind the stock. For this simple rule, it was “What direction is the P/E ratio pointing? Up or down?”. If down, then I know I do not have a wave of both institutional and retail support to push prices higher. Because of this, these companies were eliminated:

      1. MAZE, ABEV, ADI, FCFS, GLW, HAS, MSCI, NU, TSM, ZM

        1. Special shout outs to Hasbro, and Nu Holdings, . Hasbro was probably my favorite between these 2, but both had really strong charts, with upward trends, consistent higher lows and price action recently pushing 52-day highs. Trend is friend.

        2. MAZE data was more scant, since this ticker only came onto the charts January 2025. With a google search of “MAZE P/E Ratio” it showed negative…but expected growth. Regardless, I had to rank this one lower in the batch.

Before I show you the top 4 companies, 2 were still looked great, but were simply pushed down a bit because they were slightly weaker on their quarterly earnings (still great annually!). Deutsche Bank, and RTX Corporation, . I particularly love legacy financial banks, like DB, due to our StockTok ETF research we conducted. The StockTok ETF has been crushing the S&P 500 this year so far, with traditional banks leading the charge. I would have loved to put them at the top…but we can only have 1 first place company.

Subscribe now

Now…the top 4 companies…and number 1 has a volatility contraction pattern, my favorite! They were:

All of these companies have positive earnings, both annual and quarterly; positive cashflow, strong up trending charts. They are differentiated by the tiniest of details.

4th Place: Western Digital Corporation,

The only reason this stock is in 4th place, is because I (nor anyone) can time tops. This stock has been on a steady rise since April 2025. I have no idea where the top is at…and it may very well continue. But when a company has ran this long, I let it go.

3rd Place: Arista Networks,

I debated for a while between 3rd and 2nd for Arista. The stock is meeting all requirements…however the gap down on 04 November…even though it has been recovered…concerns me that in a sell off situation, it can be very painful. That said, it also gapped up on the 22nd of January. Overall, I have nothing bad to say about the company, meeting all fundamental rules, higher lows. I would strongly prefer this company at $164.94 to prove it has shaken off the Santa Slumber back in December.

2nd Place: Costamare,

The primary reason Costamare edged out Arista, is the fact that it has a slightly, very slightly, stronger relative strength at 66 indicating stronger trend relative to the rest of the market. Additionally, the gap up in May 2025 directly reminded me of all the biggest winners from the StockTok screener. It was normal for them to have sprinted up nearly a year ago…and then just quietly inched up. I nearly put it 1st place, but the winner had a distinct volatility contraction pattern on it.

1st Place: Vulcan Materials Company,

This was a surprise. An unknown name crushing basically everything. Annual cashflow increased from $664M to $806M, a 21% increase. Earnings from 7.0 to 7.53. P/E speculation rising. And a big volatility contraction pattern, VCP. Literally nothing bad I can say or critique. If price action is within +/- 5% of current price tomorrow, 04 February, I will add this to my portfolio.

Here was the final ranking and a demonstration how I crossed them off as I went.
